sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: **Craft-Centered Education** where learning is integrated around a manual productive work or craft (e.g., spinning, weaving, agriculture, carpentry) to ensure self-sufficiency and dignity of labor.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: **Mother Tongue as Medium** of instruction for all subjects at the basic education stage to facilitate cognitive absorption and cultural grounding.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: **Free and Compulsory Education** for all children aged 7 to 14 years, translating into a comprehensive 7-year basic schooling curriculum.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: **Self-Supporting Aspect**: The scheme intended that the sale of goods produced by students during vocational training would cover the running expenses of the schools, reducing financial burden on the state.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Convened in October 1937 following Gandhi's articles in Harijan; attended by prominent educationists.
Discussed and adopted core principles of Nai Talim.
Marks the formal genesis of indigenous nationalist educational planning.
Detailed blueprint committee appointed to flesh out the Wardha Scheme into a concrete syllabus.
Drafted detailed syllabi focusing on craft integration and teacher training.
Standard exam reference for the implementation structure of Basic Education.
Formal endorsement by the Indian National Congress of the Wardha Scheme.
Provincial Congress Ministries were directed to implement it.
Connects nationalist political strategy with socio-economic nation-building.

items.definition: Literally translates to 'New Education'; Gandhi's holistic philosophy combining education, livelihood, and moral development.
The expert committee tasked with translating Gandhi's ideas into a practical curriculum and pedagogical structure.
The mechanism wherein student productivity in crafts would help sustain school operational costs, though criticized as economically impractical later.
Preceded by Sargent Plan (1944) and followed by post-independence Radhakrishnan and Kothari Commission evaluations of work-experience (SUPW).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Region / Zone Details**: Implemented experimentally in Congress-governed provinces after 1937 (e.g., Central Provinces, Bombay, United Provinces, Bihar).
• **Driving Advantages**: Provincial Congress ministries provided initial administrative backing and institutional testing grounds before the resignation of ministries in 1939.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Heavy reliance on craft output created administrative hurdles, quality compromise in core academic subjects, and resistance from orthodox elites favoring bookish English education.
• **Policy Interventions**: Evolved into modern vocational education frameworks, skill India initiatives, and experiential learning models under NEP.

items.title: Mnemonic for Classification / Sequence
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'W-Z-H' (Wardha, Zakir Hussain, Haripura)
• **Decoded Meaning**: Wardha Conference (1937) -> Zakir Hussain Committee (1938) -> Haripura Session approval (1938).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly eliminates chronological confusion in matching questions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Age bracket is 7 to 14 years (7 years duration), centered on a craft, through the mother tongue.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often frames options stating that the Wardha Scheme was introduced by the British Government (e.g., through Sadler or Hunter Commission). Remember: It was entirely a nationalist, indigenous initiative conceived by Mahatma Gandhi and endorsed by the INC.

Mains Value Addition: Link Nai Talim to contemporary educational debates on vocationalization, Skill Development, NEP 2020's emphasis on experiential learning, and Gandhian ideals of decentralized rural economy.

keyTakeaways: The Wardha Scheme (1937) championed craft-centered, free, and compulsory primary education in the mother tongue.
The Zakir Hussain Committee provided the structural and pedagogical curriculum for its implementation.
Despite economic limitations of the self-supporting model, it laid the philosophical bedrock for vocational and value-based education in independent India.
